blocks.text: The **Indus/Harappan Civilisation (c. 2600–1900 BCE)** is famed for the **world's first systematic urban planning** — a **grid layout, standardised baked bricks, the citadel-lower-town division, and an unmatched covered drainage system** — evidence of a highly organised civic authority.

rows: Streets cut at **right angles (N-S / E-W)**; blocks of houses; the earliest 'town planning'.
Raised **citadel** (west) for public/ritual buildings; **lower town** (east) residential; fortified.
**Standardised burnt bricks** in a fixed **4:2:1 ratio**; kiln-fired (unlike contemporaries).
**Covered drains** along streets, house drains connected to street drains, soak-pits, manholes — the finest of the ancient world.
Watertight tank (gypsum mortar, bitumen lining); likely ritual bathing.
Large brick granaries at Harappa & Mohenjodaro — state storage.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A[Grid streets, right angles] --> B[Citadel + Lower town]
  B --> C[Burnt bricks 1:2:4]
  C --> D[Covered drains + soak pits]
  D --> E[Great Bath, granary, Lothal dockyard]

items: Uniform **burnt-brick ratio 1:2:4** and a covered **drainage system** are the two most-tested planning facts.
The **Great Bath** (Mohenjo-daro) = ritual bathing; **granaries** = surplus storage; **no temples/palaces** identified.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: planning, materials & architecture

items: **Grid/chessboard plan**: streets cut at **right angles** (N-S & E-W); the main street at Mohenjo-daro ran ~**9 m wide**.
**Two-part city**: raised **citadel** (west — public buildings) + **lower town** (east — residential); both often **fortified**.
**Burnt-brick** construction with standard ratio **4:2:1** (L:B:H) — same across sites = central standardisation; kiln-fired bricks (Mesopotamia used mud-brick).

**Drainage** was the civilisation's hallmark: covered brick drains with **manholes/soak-pits**, house drains connecting to street drains — 'no other Bronze-Age culture gave such attention to health & cleanliness' (Marshall).
**Great Bath** (Mohenjo-daro): 12×7×2.4 m tank, made watertight with **gypsum mortar & bitumen**, changing rooms, a well to fill it, drain to empty — **ritual bathing**.
**Great Granary**: Mohenjo-daro's largest structure; Harappa had a series of granaries near the river with brick platforms.
**Houses**: courtyard-centred, private **wells & bathrooms**, staircases (upper storeys), **doors on side lanes** (not main street) for privacy; no windows facing streets.

rows: Possibly non-monarchical / mercantile-council rule; unusually egalitarian layout
A central authority enforcing uniformity over 1.3 million sq km
Ritual/religious use of water — continuity into later Hindu practice

items: Remember the trio: grid streets, standardised bricks (4:2:1), and covered drainage — the exam's favourite IVC facts.
Great Bath (Mohenjodaro), Great Granary, and the citadel/lower-town split are frequent MCQ points.

Dockyard at **Lothal**; 'Lower Town' with warehouses; no clearly identified temples/palaces.
Fortifications & the 'Great Granary' show a strong central civic authority.
Grid pattern = **chessboard** layout; houses had private wells & bathrooms.
Dholavira uniquely shows a **three-part** city and elaborate **water reservoirs**.

blocks.text: Harappan society was **urban, seemingly egalitarian and trade-driven**, resting on a **surplus agrarian economy, standardised weights, and extensive internal and long-distance trade** reaching **Mesopotamia (Meluhha)**.

rows: Wheat, barley, peas, sesame, mustard, cotton (**first to grow cotton — 'Sindon'**); ploughed fields at Kalibangan.
Humped cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat; **no conclusive evidence of the horse**.
Bead-making (Chanhudaro, Lothal), shell, metallurgy (bronze — copper+tin), pottery (red-black).
**Binary then decimal** system (16 and multiples); standardised cubical chert weights.
**Steatite seals** (~2000 found) used in trade; Persian Gulf seals abroad.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: society, economy & trade

items: **Society**: urban, orderly; likely **matriarchal leanings** (abundant mother-goddess figurines); occupational differentiation (traders, artisans, farmers); no clear evidence of an army or warfare.

**Agriculture**: wheat, barley (staples), **cotton (first in the world — Greeks called it *Sindon*)**, peas, sesame, mustard, dates; **rice** at Lothal/Rangpur; used wooden ploughs (Kalibangan field).
**Domesticated animals**: humped bull (zebu), buffalo, sheep, goat, pig, elephant, dog, cat; **horse** absent/debated (key exam point); camel bones at Kalibangan.
**Crafts & industry**: bead-making (Lothal, Chanhudaro), shell/ivory work, metallurgy (copper, bronze, gold, silver — **not iron**), pottery (wheel-made, red-and-black), faience, seal-cutting.

**Trade** (internal + external): with **Mesopotamia (Meluhha), Oman (Magan), Bahrain (Dilmun)**; Harappan seals & etched carnelian beads found in Mesopotamia; imports — copper (Khetri/Oman), gold (Karnataka), lapis lazuli (Afghanistan), turquoise, jade.

**Trade mechanism**: **barter** (no coins); regulated by **standard weights** (cubical chert; ratios 1,2,4,8,16…320 — binary then decimal); Lothal **dockyard** = maritime hub; bullock carts & boats for transport.
Cotton ('Sindon'), no horse, Meluhha/Dilmun/Magan trade route, and standardised weights are the recurring MCQ facts.
Bead & metal craft centres: Chanhudaro & Lothal.

prelimsPointers: IVC people were the **first to produce cotton** — Greeks called it **'Sindon'**.

**Chanhudaro & Lothal** — bead-making centres; **Lothal** — dockyard (maritime trade).
Metallurgy — **bronze (copper+tin)**; aware of gold, silver, copper, lead; **not iron** (pre-iron age).
Trade was largely **barter**; ~2000 **steatite seals** aided commerce.
**Cotton** first cultivated by Harappans (Greek *Sindon*); **rice** at Lothal/Rangpur.
**Horse absent/debated**; trade with **Meluhha=Indus, Magan=Oman, Dilmun=Bahrain**.
Weights **cubical chert**, binary→decimal (1,2,4,8,16…); **barter**, no coins.
Copper from **Khetri**; gold from **Kolar**; lapis lazuli from **Afghanistan**.

blocks.text: Harappan art is **small-scale, realistic and masterly** — the **bronze 'Dancing Girl', the steatite 'Priest-King', terracotta figurines, and the iconic seals (esp. the Pashupati seal)** — reflecting advanced metallurgy (lost-wax casting) and craftsmanship.

rows: Mohenjodaro; three-faced figure surrounded by animals ('proto-Shiva').
The **humped bull** and **unicorn** are common seal motifs.
Mother-goddess figurines, toys, bullock carts; the **'first bronze sculpture' tradition**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: art, seals & crafts

items: **Seals** (~2000 found): mostly **steatite**, square, ~2.5 cm; a **pictograph + animal** motif; the **'unicorn'** is commonest; the **Pashupati seal** shows a horned yogi with animals; used for **trade/property marking** (stamped on clay tags).
**Bronze sculpture**: **Dancing Girl** (Mohenjo-daro) — **lost-wax (cire perdue)** casting, tribal features, bangles; bronze buffalo & bullock-cart.
**Stone sculpture**: steatite **'Priest-King'** (trefoil robe, headband, half-closed eyes), bearded man; red-sandstone **male torso** (Harappa); grey stone dancing figure.
**Terracotta**: mother-goddess figurines, toys (whistles, carts), animal figures; **red-and-black painted pottery** (wheel-turned).

**Ornaments**: beads of carnelian, agate, steatite, gold, faience; **Lothal & Chanhudaro** = bead-manufacturing hubs; the famous **'necklace'** and micro-drilled long carnelian beads (a Harappan trade specialty).
**Metals used**: copper, bronze, gold, silver, lead — **iron unknown**; bronze via copper+tin alloying.

blocks.text: Prelims trap: the **Dancing Girl is bronze (lost-wax); the Priest-King is steatite (stone)**. Seals are chiefly **steatite**. Don't mix these materials up.

items: Dancing Girl = bronze (lost-wax); Priest-King = steatite; Pashupati seal = 'proto-Shiva' — the three must-know artefacts.
Seals are mostly steatite, square, with the unicorn/humped-bull motif and undeciphered script.

**Dancing Girl = bronze (lost-wax)**; **Priest-King = steatite**; most **seals = steatite**.
Commonest seal animal = **'unicorn'**; bull, elephant, rhino, tiger also depicted (no horse).
**Lothal & Chanhudaro** = bead-making centres; iron **unknown** to IVC.

blocks.text: Harappan **religion** centred on a **Mother-Goddess, a proto-Shiva (Pashupati), and nature/animal worship**; the **script remains undeciphered**; and the civilisation's **decline (c. 1900 BCE)** is explained by multiple theories — climate/river change being most favoured today.

rows: No monumental temples/idols clearly identified; ritual at the Great Bath.
Mostly **extended inhumation** (N-S); cemetery R-37 (Harappa); pot burials.
**Aryan invasion (Wheeler — now discredited), floods (Mohenjodaro), river drying (Ghaggar-Hakra/Saraswati), climate change/aridity, ecological degradation, decline of trade**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: religion, script & decline

items: **Religion**: **Mother Goddess** (fertility) worship; **proto-Shiva / Pashupati** (three-faced horned deity, seated in yogic posture, surrounded by animals); **phallus (lingam) & yoni** worship; **pipal/peepal tree** & animal worship (bull, unicorn); **fire-altars** (Kalibangan, Lothal) suggest ritual sacrifice; **no temples**, no priestly class evidenced.
**Continuity with Hinduism**: Pashupati→Shiva, lingam worship, pipal veneration, tank/ritual bathing, swastika motif — many later Hindu elements have Harappan roots.
**Burial practices**: mostly **extended inhumation** (N-S); Cemetery R-37 & H (Harappa); some fractional & pot burials; grave goods modest = relatively egalitarian.

**Decline theories**: (1) **climate change/aridification** (Fairservis), (2) **Aryan invasion** (Wheeler — 'massacre at Mohenjo-daro', now discredited), (3) **floods & river shift/tectonics** (M.R. Sahni, R.L. Raikes), (4) **Saraswati (Ghaggar-Hakra) drying up**, (5) **decline of trade with Mesopotamia**, (6) **ecological degradation/deforestation, salinity**. Consensus: a **gradual, multi-causal de-urbanisation**, not sudden collapse.

rows: Floods & tectonic uplift damming the Indus

items: Mother-Goddess + Pashupati + pipal/animal worship = religion; undeciphered pictographic script; multi-causal decline (climate/river most accepted).
Wheeler's Aryan-invasion theory of decline is now largely rejected.

blocks.text: The **Early/Rig Vedic Age (c. 1500–1000 BCE)** was a **pastoral, tribal, largely egalitarian society** of Indo-Aryans in the **Sapta-Sindhu (land of seven rivers)**. Cattle were the measure of wealth; the polity was **kin-based (tribal), not territorial**; and society had **no rigid caste or untouchability**.

rows: **Tribal (jana), not territorial**; chief = **Rajan** (protector of cattle); assemblies **Sabha & Samiti** (and Vidatha, Gana).
**Pastoral & cattle-centred** — cow ('**Gomat**') = wealth; ' **Gavishti**' (search for cows) = war; some agriculture.
**Patriarchal but women respected** (Gargi, Lopamudra, Apala); **no rigid varna/untouchability**; family (kula) basis.
**Nature worship** — **Indra (most hymns), Agni, Varuna, Soma**; yajna (sacrifice); no temples/idols.
**Rig Veda** — oldest (1028 hymns, 10 mandalas); **Gayatri mantra** (to Savitri) in 3rd mandala.

blocks.text: The engine of change was **iron + the plough** — surplus agriculture turned a pastoral tribal society into a caste-stratified territorial monarchy.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Rig Vedic polity, society & economy

items: **Sources**: the **Rigveda** (1028 hymns, 10 mandalas; II–VII = 'family books', oldest; X = latest, has Purusha Sukta). Archaeology: **Painted Grey Ware** overlaps Later Vedic.

**Polity**: **tribal (jana), semi-nomadic, kinship-based**; the **Rajan (chief)** led in war & protection, not an absolute king; assisted by **Purohita (priest — Vasishtha, Vishwamitra), Senani (war), Gramani (village)**. Two assemblies: **Sabha** (elders/nobles) & **Samiti** (whole tribe, elected the Rajan); also **Vidatha & Gana**.

**Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna)**: on the **Parushni (Ravi)**, Bharata king **Sudas** (with Vasishtha) defeated a confederacy of ten tribes — the most important political event of the Rig Vedic age.

**Society**: **patriarchal but not rigid**; **varna** was occupation-based & flexible (the fourfold order appears only in the late **Purusha Sukta, X.90**); **women** respected — educated (**Gargi, Lopamudra, Apala, Ghosha, Maitreyi**), attended assemblies, no sati/child-marriage/purdah.

**Economy**: **pastoral — cattle (gau) = chief wealth & unit of value**; 'Gavishti/Gavesana' (search for cows) = term for war; **barter** (cow, later **nishka** gold ornament); limited agriculture (barley = *yava*); river-based; **Panis** = trader/hoarder foes; no coins, no cities.
Cattle-pastoral economy, tribal (not territorial) polity, Sabha/Samiti, Indra-Agni-Varuna worship — the core Rig Vedic facts.
Contrast with the Later Vedic (HC-008): territorial kingdoms, agriculture, rigid varna.

prelimsPointers: Rig Veda — **oldest Veda**; **1028 hymns, 10 mandalas**; books 2–7 the 'family books' (oldest).

**Sapta-Sindhu** — land of seven rivers; **Saraswati** the most revered river.

**Cattle = wealth**; war = **'Gavishti'** (search for cows); **Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna)** on the Parushni (Ravi).
**No untouchability / rigid caste**; women could attend Sabha; women seers — **Gargi, Lopamudra, Apala, Ghosha**.
**Gayatri mantra** (to Savitri) is in the **3rd mandala** (Vishwamitra).

Rig Vedic economy = **pastoral/cattle (gau = wealth)**; 'Gavishti' (search for cattle) = war.
Rigveda = **1028 hymns, 10 mandalas**; books **II–VII oldest**; **Purusha Sukta (X.90)** = varna origin (latest).
**Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna)** on the **Parushni (Ravi)** — **Sudas (Bharata)** won.
Cattle = wealth; **Gavishti** = war; **Nishka** = gold currency; Sabha & Samiti were powerful.

blocks.text: The **Later Vedic Age (c. 1000–600 BCE)** saw the shift to the **Ganga plains, iron use ('Krishna Ayas'), settled agriculture, larger territorial kingdoms (janapadas), a rigid varna order, and the rise of elaborate rituals** — the world captured in the later Vedic literature.

rows: **Territorial kingdoms (janapada/rashtra)**; king's power grows (**Rajasuya, Ashvamedha, Vajapeya** sacrifices); Sabha/Samiti decline.
**Iron ('Shyama/Krishna Ayas')**, plough agriculture, rice/wheat; PGW pottery.
**Rigid four-fold varna** hardens; **untouchability & patriarchy** deepen; **four ashramas** emerge.
**Prajapati, Vishnu, Rudra** rise; **ritualism/sacrifice dominates**; reaction later via Upanishads.
**Rig (hymns), Sama (melodies — roots of music), Yajur (rituals), Atharva (magic/charms)**.
Earliest Vedic text, 1028 hymns, praises Indra, Agni
Collection of hymns for rituals, basis of Indian classical music
Procedures for yajnas, divided into Krishna & Shukla Yajurveda

blocks.text: The two civilisations contrasted (a perennial prelims MCQ):

Indigenous origin, possibly influenced by Mesopotamia

Tribal kings (Rajan), later evolved into hereditary monarchy

Iron Age civilization (iron tools for agriculture, warfare)
No major evidence of warfare, peaceful society

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Later Vedic change & Vedic literature

items: **Later Vedic (1000–600 BCE)**: composed the **Sama, Yajur, Atharva Vedas + Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads**; PGW + **iron ('krishna-ayas/shyama')** archaeology; centre shifts to the **Ganga-Yamuna doab (Kuru-Panchala)**.

**Polity**: tribal chief → **territorial king (Rajan)**; larger units — **Rashtra, Janapada**; kings performed **Rajasuya, Ashvamedha, Vajapeya** for legitimacy & divinity; **Sabha & Samiti declined**; new officials (**Bhagadugha** revenue-collector, **Sangrahitri** treasurer).
**Society**: **four-fold varna rigid & birth-based**; **gotra** appears; **four ashramas** (later); **women's status fell** — excluded from assemblies & upanayana, early hints of sub-ordination.
**Economy**: **agriculture central** (iron ploughshare, rice = *vrihi*), private land, expanding crafts, early trade & the **nishka/satamana** as money precursors.

**Religion**: nature gods declined; **Prajapati (creator), Vishnu, Rudra-Shiva** rise; **ritualism & sacrifice** peaked; reaction → **Upanishadic philosophy** (Atman-Brahman, karma, rebirth, moksha; 'Satyameva Jayate' — Mundaka).

rows: The 4 Vedas — Rig (hymns), Sama (melodies/music), Yajur (rituals; Shukla & Krishna), Atharva (spells, medicine, folk).
108 in number; Vedanta — Atman, Brahman, karma, moksha.
6 limbs — Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda, Jyotisha.

items: Iron + agriculture + territorial kingdoms + rigid varna + big royal sacrifices = Later Vedic transformation.
Veda order: Rig→Sama→Yajur→Atharva; Sama = origins of Indian music; Upanishads = Vedanta (end of Vedas).
